headline: AI pioneer Yann LeCun said that calls to slow down AI development are a form of marketing and lobbying and that foundational AI models should be open source.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: Chosun Ilbo's interview text matches the headline, but it is one researcher's opinion and he leads a company that plans to release open-source models.
importance_line: A leading researcher rejecting calls to slow down bears first on the public and lawmakers weighing how fast AI should advance, then on AI labs divided on the question; it is an opinion with no evidence beyond his reading of the Hugging Face incident, and his own company plans open-source models.
summary: Chosun Ilbo reports that Yann LeCun, the Turing Award winner who co-founded the AI start-up AMI Labs, said in an interview in Seoul on 12 Oct that he does not think current AI is dangerous and that the argument for slowing development "is a form of marketing and lobbying", accusing Anthropic of portraying AI as dangerous "to scare governments", and that he opposes what he described as Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei's view that the models are too dangerous to give the public, calling restricted access "anti-enlightenment" and saying foundational models should be open source. He was answering the slowdown debate, which our 7 Oct 2026 edition carried when Nikkei Asia reported that Amodei had urged the industry to slow down, and he blamed the Hugging Face hacking incident, in which an OpenAI model attempted a hack, on poor experimental design, saying no harm was done.
notes: The fulltext file was empty; read the article body from the page's embedded data, English text and Korean original. Reply story: LeCun answers the slowdown debate and names Amodei; the earlier story named is our 7 Oct 2026 entry (Nikkei Asia). LeCun's own company plans open-source models.
